title: Bunsen Burner

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: A gas-fueled open flame used in microbiology labs primarily to create a localized sterile field by convection and to flame-sterilize inoculating loops/needles and tube mouths as part of aseptic technique.
operatingPrinciple: Fuel gas mixes with air at an adjustable intake collar before combusting at the burner tip; adjusting the air intake changes the flame from a cooler, yellow, sooty flame (low air) to a hotter, near-invisible blue flame (higher air) suited for sterilizing work.
basicOperation: Connect the burner to the gas supply and confirm no leaks before igniting.
Open the gas valve slightly and ignite with a spark lighter or match, not an open flame source held close to the hand.
Adjust the air intake collar until a well-defined blue inner cone is visible — this is the hottest, cleanest part of the flame.
Work within the flame's convection zone (the rising warm air envelope around it) to reduce airborne contamination during aseptic transfers.
Turn off the gas fully at the valve when finished, not just by extinguishing the visible flame.
importantSettings: Air intake collar position (controls flame color/temperature and cleanliness of combustion)
maintenance: Keep the burner tip clean and free of debris that could distort the flame shape.
Check gas tubing periodically for cracking or brittleness and replace as needed.

commonErrors.cause: Insufficient air intake, causing incomplete combustion
commonErrors.fix: Open the air intake collar until a clean blue flame with a visible inner cone appears

commonErrors.cause: Excessive air intake relative to gas flow, or a partially blocked tip
commonErrors.fix: Reduce air intake slightly and check the tip for obstruction

safety: Never leave a lit burner unattended.
Tie back loose hair and secure loose sleeves before working near the flame.
Keep flammable materials (paper, solvents) well away from the flame.
Turn off the gas supply fully, not just the visible flame, when finished.
